summary: Build “Your Desk Pet”: a lightweight desktop productivity/pomodoro app-game with a persistent on-screen virtual pet (cat or dog) that reacts in real time to focus/procrastination and rewards completed sessions with positive interactions (feeding/grooming/petting).
architectural_notes: Pet art style: simple pixel art characters (cat and dog).
Emotional design constraint: roasts are playful, not abusive; focus on emotional payoff over points-heavy gamification.
Overlay requirement: pet remains persistently visible on screen during focus sessions; animations should be subtle to avoid distraction.
Pet overlay presentation: render as a single pet figure (minimal chrome) and persist across in-app screen navigation (overlay mounted above route changes).
Home screen visual direction: pixel-art playground landscape background with pets playing (keep subtle to avoid distraction).
known_issues: Pet overlay is not following the user as expected (pet does not track the user during use).
App/icon is showing multiple pets instead of a single pet (should display only one pet).
imageRequirements:
## Required Images
- Pixel-art app icon depicting a single pet (cat) centered on a transparent or solid background (app-icon-cat.dim_512x512.png)
- Pixel-art app icon depicting a single pet (dog) centered on a transparent or solid background (app-icon-dog.dim_512x512.png)
- Pixel-art favicon depicting a single pet (cat) simplified for small sizes (favicon-cat.dim_64x64.png)
- Pixel-art favicon depicting a single pet (dog) simplified for small sizes (favicon-dog.dim_64x64.png)

existing_features.title: Implement the core “Set Focus Time” flow: allow the user to select a pet (Cat or Dog), configure focus duration and break duration, optionally enable repeating break cycles, and optionally enter a task list for the session.

Create an “Active Focus Session” screen with a persistent on-screen pet overlay area that remains visible while the user uses the app, with subtle idle animations and a visible countdown timer for the focus phase.
Implement a mood system and visual mood indicator tied to user “focus behavior” during the focus phase, with escalating states based on procrastination/interruption duration.

Add in-app “behavior monitoring” signals that can drive procrastination detection without relying on OS-level app monitoring: support (a) inactivity detection (no mouse/keyboard interaction in the page for N minutes), (b) tab/app visibility change detection (page hidden/visible), and (c) manual check-ins (“I got distracted”) plus a user-configurable list of “wasted time platforms” as labels used in manual check-ins.

Implement a tiered dialogue system with personality-specific tone and escalation rules: Cat delivers judgmental/passive-aggressive lines, Dog delivers needy/supportive lines that become progressively roast-y; dialogues escalate based on accumulated procrastination duration and can also show a distinct completion line at focus completion.

Implement the “Session Completion” and “Reward State” flow: when the focus timer completes, unlock feeding interaction during the break phase, show positive pet animations/affirmations during the configured break time, and optionally allow additional simple interactions (groom/pet/play) during break.

Persist user configuration and lightweight session history: store pet choice, default focus/break durations, wasted-platform labels, and a simple log of completed focus sessions (timestamp + duration + pet) for optional progress/consistency viewing.
Apply a coherent, playful pixel-desktop visual theme across the app (colors, typography, layout) that fits a light productivity game and is enforced consistently across screens.

Add generated pixel-art static assets (cat, dog, and simple UI/reward sprites) and render them in the pet overlay, mood states, and feeding/reward interactions using files stored under frontend/public/assets/generated.

Update the PetOverlay UI so the floating pet “pop up” visually reads as a single animal figure rather than a large panel/card. Remove the large bordered container styling and keep only the pet sprite (and optional small controls), while preserving the speech bubble positioning and pixel-art rendering.

Make the pet overlay persist across app screen navigation while a session is active: when the user switches between screens (e.g., Home/Setup, Progress, Focus, Break) during an ongoing focus/break session, the pet overlay remains visible without disappearing.

Ensure the underlying session state continues correctly when navigating away from the focus/break screens (i.e., session timers and phase transitions should not reset just because the user navigated to another screen).

Generate a new pixel-art style Home page background image depicting a playground landscape with pets playing in the distance (no UI text embedded in the image). Store it as a static asset under frontend/public/assets/generated and ensure it can be referenced from React via a stable public path.

Apply the new playground landscape background to the Home (session setup) screen in a way that preserves readability and the existing pixel-desktop theme. The background must not interfere with interactions (forms/buttons) and must not obscure the persistent PetOverlay when a session is active.

Make the app end-to-end functional by ensuring the complete flow works without runtime errors for both authenticated and unauthenticated states: login (Internet Identity) → profile setup (if missing) → start session → focus timer → transition to break → save completed session to backend → view session history in Progress, with graceful handling when the user is not logged in (no unauthorized traps causing a broken UI).

Use saved user settings (focus duration, break duration, wasted platforms) to prefill and synchronize the Home/Setup experience and distraction check-ins, so the default configuration is consistent across Home and Progress Settings.

Fix the PetOverlay so the pet visually follows the user during an active session (the overlay position should track the user’s pointer/movement within the page rather than feeling ‘stuck’ in one corner). Maintain non-blocking behavior (do not interfere with page interactions) and keep the overlay fully on-screen.

Fix sprite rendering in PetOverlay so only one pet frame is visible at a time (do not show the entire sprite sheet). Ensure the speech bubble and mute icon remain correctly positioned relative to the single visible pet frame.

Update the app’s favicon/app icon so it displays a single pet (not multiple pets/frames). Use a pixel-art single-pet icon and ensure it is used by the browser tab (and any manifest/PWA icon configuration present in the project).

new_feature_requests.summary: Pomodoro-style focus + break session setup (custom durations) with optional break cycles and goals
Task list support tied to focus sessions (optional tasks)
Persistent always-on-top/floating desktop overlay that shows the pet during sessions with subtle animations
User behavior monitoring during focus (e.g., inactivity, app switching, manual check-ins) with configurable “wasted time” platforms
Pet mood system with visual indicator and mood changes tied to user behavior/procrastination duration
Tiered dialogue system with personality-specific tone (cat: judgmental; dog: needy) and escalation based on time wasted
Session completion reward interactions (feed; optionally groom/pet/play) during break with positive animations/affirmations
Backend: add Motoko canister methods to support saving/loading per-user settings and appending/querying session history (completed focus sessions).
Refine pet overlay UI: show as a single animal figure (not a larger panel) and keep it persistent/visible when navigating between app screens
Home page background art: playground landscape with pets playing in the background (fits pixel theme)
Make the app end-to-end functional: ensure the full user flow works from session setup → active focus → break/rewards → persistence/history without broken navigation/state
